# cosmo_contract (Resource)

A contract is a Terraform resource representing a single subgraph with GraphQL Federation enabled, allowing developers to build versatile, multi-audience graphs while simplifying development and ensuring maintainability. 

For more information, refer to the Cosmo Documentation at https://cosmo-docs.wundergraph.com/concepts/schema-contracts.

## Creating a contract before the source graph has any subgraphs

Cosmo only creates a contract once its source graph has composed successfully, and a graph only composes once
at least one subgraph has published a schema with a Query field. So a contract normally can't be created in
the same apply as a brand-new federated graph.

Setting `create_temp_subgraph_if_needed = true` works around this. When the contract is created, and only
then, the provider checks the source graph. If the graph has not composed and none of its subgraphs has a
published schema, the provider:

1. creates a subgraph named `temp-contract-bootstrap-<contract name>`, with labels that the source graph's
   label matchers accept (or no labels, if the source graph has no label matchers), and a routing URL on the
   reserved `.invalid` domain;
2. publishes a schema with a single field, `Query._tempContractBootstrap`, whose comments explain why it
   exists. The field carries the contract's `include_tags`, so the contract composes too;
3. creates the contract;
4. deletes the temporary subgraph.

In every other case the contract is created as usual, and the setting does nothing.

By default the provider refuses, and changes nothing, if publishing or deleting the temporary subgraph would
also recompose any graph or contract other than the source graph. That includes existing contracts of the
source graph, so by default only one contract per empty source graph can be created this way. Set
`allow_recomposing_other_graphs = true` to allow it.

~> **Warning** Read this before using `create_temp_subgraph_if_needed`:

- **The dummy schema stays visible.** Once the temporary subgraph is deleted, the source graph has nothing to
  compose, and Cosmo keeps its last successful composition, which is the dummy one. Routers for the source graph
  and the contract receive a schema containing only `_tempContractBootstrap` (queries to it fail) until a
  real subgraph is published. Cosmo Studio's composition history and changelog keep the dummy entries permanently.
- **An interrupted apply can leave the subgraph behind.** The provider still deletes the subgraph when Terraform
  is stopped with a single Ctrl-C or a graceful pipeline cancel, but not if the process is killed. A leftover is
  reported as a warning on every plan for the contract, and is deleted the next time the contract is created.
  You can also delete it yourself in Cosmo Studio or with `wgc subgraph delete <name> -n <namespace>`.
- **The API key needs more access.** It must be allowed to create, publish and delete subgraphs in the
  namespace, and to see **every** graph in it. Cosmo hides graphs the key can't see, and the provider can only
  protect the graphs it can see. The temporary subgraph also counts towards your plan's subgraph limit, and any
  admission webhook on the source graph is called.
- **Graphs created at the same time aren't protected.** A graph created in the namespace while the temporary
  subgraph exists (by someone else, or by another resource in the same apply) can pick it up. Use
  `depends_on` so that the contract is created after the other graphs in the same configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cosmo_contract" "test" {
  name         = var.name
  namespace    = var.namespace
  source       = var.source_graph_name
  routing_url  = var.routing_url
  exclude_tags = var.exclude_tags
  include_tags = var.include_tags
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)
- `namespace` (String)
- `routing_url` (String)
- `source` (String)

### Optional

- `admission_webhook_secret` (String)
- `admission_webhook_url` (String)
- `allow_recomposing_other_graphs` (Boolean) Only used with `create_temp_subgraph_if_needed`. If `false` (the default), the provider refuses to use a temporary subgraph if that would recompose any graph or contract other than the source graph. If `true`, it goes ahead anyway and lists what was recomposed in a warning. **Dangerous:** a recomposed graph that is in use briefly serves the dummy `_tempContractBootstrap` field to its routers, and is recomposed again when the temporary subgraph is deleted. Existing contracts of the source graph count as other graphs, so this must be `true` to create a second contract this way while the source graph is still empty.
- `create_temp_subgraph_if_needed` (Boolean) If `true`, and the source graph has not composed and has no subgraph with a published schema when this contract is created, the provider creates the contract with the help of a temporary subgraph, which it deletes again straight afterwards. Defaults to `false`. Only used when the contract is created; changing it later has no effect. **Leaves a dummy schema on the source graph's and the contract's routers until a real subgraph is published.** See [Creating a contract before the source graph has any subgraphs](#creating-a-contract-before-the-source-graph-has-any-subgraphs) for how it works and its risks.
- `exclude_tags` (List of String)
- `include_tags` (List of String)
- `readme` (String)
- `supports_federation` (Boolean)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Contracts can be imported using the UUID of the contract, e.g.
terraform import cosmo_contract.example 0b1b1b1b-1b1b-1b1b-1b1b-1b1b1b1b1b1b
```
